events.title: Graydon Hoare begins Rust
events.summary: Graydon Hoare began [Rust] as a personal project in July 2006 (initial commit July 23) — [Mozilla] sponsorship followed in 2009, turning it into a research language for safe systems programming.
events.about: Hoare designed [Rust]'s ownership model to eliminate memory bugs without [garbage collection]. [Mozilla] sponsored [Rust] until community foundations took over — now used in Linux, browsers, and infrastructure.

narrative.whyChosen: [Rust]'s ownership model is the most influential memory-safety idea since [garbage collection].
narrative.whyImportant: It offered a third path between manual C and GC languages.
narrative.problemSolved: Systems programmers needed safety without runtime overhead or GC pauses.
